financials.source: Form 990 FY2024 via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (EIN 41-0991680; note: the EIN 41-0695635 in this file could not be verified — Fairview Health Services files under 41-0991680). Total revenue and total assets from Form 990. Operating income (~$51M) and operating margin (<1%) from Star Tribune and MedCity News reporting on FY2024 audited consolidated financial statements (first operating profit since 2018 on ~$8B audited operating revenue). Form 990 revenue ($5.33B) differs from audited GAAP operating revenue (~$8B) due to reporting methodology differences. Audited FY2025/2024 statements published April 2026 at fairview.org.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: FY2023 audited consolidated financial statements (short-term investments $466,989K + long-term investments $1,460,835K; total investments per note disclosure $2,007,675K including equity-method and NAV-measured holdings). FY2022: $1,935,426K. FY2024 investment figures require verification from FY2025/2024 audited statements published April 2026.
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: Fairview operates 12 hospitals and 100+ clinics across Minnesota; real estate value not separately broken out in available filings
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Total net assets FY2023: $2,057,673K (Fairview Health Services $1,973,274K + non-controlling interests $48,802K + donor-restricted $35,597K). Assets limited as to use reported separately (insurance subsidiaries $55,958K and restricted fund investments $18,687K in FY2022). Board-designated and endowment sub-totals require Form 990 Part X or note disclosure verification.

bondDebt.source: FY2023 audited consolidated financial statements (~$1.52B total debt, down from ~$1.55B in FY2022). Key tax-exempt series: 2018A ($263.9M original proceeds via City of Minneapolis, refunding + $100M new money), 2017A (2.00-5.00%, maturing 2047, ~$176M at FY2022), 2015A (2.00-5.00%, maturing 2044, ~$95M at FY2022). Also 3.456% taxable bonds maturing Nov 2051 (~$100.9M per CBonds). Moody's cited ~$1.6B total debt at time of Baa1 downgrade. Current outstanding balances require verification from most recent EMMA continuing disclosure or FY2025/2024 audited statements.

executiveComp.source: Form 990 FY2024 Part VII via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (EIN 41-0991680). Reportable compensation from organization: $4,854,478; reportable from related organizations: $0; estimated other compensation: $805,007; total: $5,659,485. FY2023 total: $5,246,751 ($5,208,444 reportable + $38,307 other). FY2022 total: $3,370,758 (included ~$1.4M bonus/incentive per Star Tribune despite operating losses; board used discretion). Bonus/incentive breakdown and deferred comp not separately itemized in available 990 data; requires Schedule J verification.

communityBenefit.source: Fairview Community Impact Report FY2024: $1.4B total community investment, of which $680M classified as community benefit (charity care, education/training, hospital-based research, community programs/services). FY2025 report: $1.6B total, $740M community benefit. Fairview notes methodology differs from Form 990 Schedule H; 990 figures may differ. Charity care sub-total and cost-adjusted amounts require Schedule H verification. Minnesota state average comparison requires Minnesota Department of Health hospital data.

taxAdvantage.notes: Fairview Health Services operates 12 hospitals and 100+ clinics as a tax-exempt nonprofit across Minnesota. Property tax exemptions span Hennepin, Ramsey, Dakota, Washington, and other Minnesota counties. Federal and state income tax exemptions, tax-exempt bond interest subsidies, and 340B program benefits all require quantification from financial statements and county assessor records.

layoffs.source: Fairview Health Services restructuring announcement September 2022; Star Tribune; Becker's Hospital Review; layoffs were part of broader cost reduction initiative amid significant operating losses

Fairview announced elimination of 250 positions in November 2023, citing inflation, labor costs, and insurer payment rates; less than 1% of workforce; included ~50% reduction in staff chaplains at metropolitan locations and security staff cuts; MPR News, Fox 9, Becker's Hospital Review, CBS Minnesota

keyRiskFactors: Five consecutive years of operating losses (2019-2023) totaling over $900M before first operating profit in 2024
Moody's downgraded from A3 to Baa1 (January 2023); S&P downgraded from A to BBB+ (February 2023)
Failed merger with Sanford Health collapsed in November 2023 amid opposition from University of Minnesota, employees, legislators, and community groups
University of Minnesota Board of Regents voted to restructure 27-year academic medicine partnership; new 10-year deal finalized January 2026 with M Health Fairview brand phaseout by end of 2026
Competitive Minneapolis-St. Paul healthcare market with Mayo Clinic, Allina Health, HealthPartners, and CentraCare
~$1.5B total debt outstanding with Baa1/BBB+ ratings (lowest investment-grade tier)
creditRating.source: Moody's: Baa1 with negative outlook (January 2023 downgrade from A3), revised to stable in 2024 citing expected improvement in operating cash flow margins. S&P: BBB+ with stable outlook (February 2023 downgrade from A). Fitch does not rate Fairview. Bond Buyer, Becker's Hospital Review, Star Tribune.

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Fairview holds ~$2.01B in investments (FY2023 audited) against ~$51M operating income (FY2024). The investment portfolio is 39x the operating profit, meaning the system's accumulated financial wealth vastly exceeds its slim operating margin. Years of operating losses (2019-2023) were sustained by this balance sheet cushion.
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Fairview carries ~$1.52B in total debt (FY2023) against $680M in claimed community benefit (FY2024). For every dollar of community benefit, the system carries $2.24 in debt — reflecting significant financial leverage. However, Fairview's community benefit methodology differs from Form 990 Schedule H; actual 990-reported community benefit may be lower.
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Charity care sub-total not separately broken out in available data. Fairview reports $680M total community benefit (FY2024) but does not publicly disclose charity care as a separate line. Minnesota state average comparison requires Minnesota Department of Health hospital data and Form 990 Schedule H Part I charity care figure.

accusation: M Health Fairview, a $5.3B-revenue tax-exempt health system, holds a $2.01B investment portfolio and carries $1.52B in bond debt while its CEO James Hereford collected $5.66M in total compensation (FY2024) — even after five consecutive years of operating losses (2019-2023) that triggered 1,150 layoffs across 2022-2023, credit downgrades to Baa1/BBB+ (lowest investment-grade tier), and the collapse of its Sanford Health merger. Fairview claims $680M in community benefit (FY2024) but uses a self-defined methodology that differs from its Form 990 reporting, and charity care as a standalone figure remains undisclosed. The system partners with the Minnesota Vikings as an official healthcare sponsor while the University of Minnesota moves to dissolve the M Health Fairview brand by end of 2026.
